claims.paper_evidence: This is a straightforward information extraction task: the LLM identifies whether specific target organ names (esophagus, thyroid gland, trachea, oral cavity) appear in the context of explicit invasion statements. The main subtlety is distinguishing “thyroid gland” (the endocrine organ) from “thyroid cartilage” (the laryngeal structure), which is handled through targeted prompt design. Specifically, the prompt is: “Identify which of the following structures are explicitly described as invaded by the tumor: [esophagus, thyroid gland, trachea, oral cavity]. Only include structures with positive invasion statements; exclude negations. Note: thyroid gland (endocrine organ) and thyroid cartilage (laryngeal structure) are different. Return a JSON list of invaded organs.”
claims.reason: Section III-D-1, first paragraph. The paper describes using an LLM with prompt engineering to extract structured invasion information for the target organs, excluding negations and distinguishing thyroid gland from thyroid cartilage.
